description:
Nuestro objetivo es desarrollar una solución tecnológica integral basada en el análisis y la visualización de datos geoespaciales de la superficie marciana para asistir en la planeación de futuras caminatas (Marswalks) y exploraciones humanas.

Estamos buscando integrar tecnologías de desarrollo de software, estructuración de datos y visualización interactiva. Si te apasiona la programación, el análisis de datos o la ciencia espacial, ¡únete a nuestro equipo para romperla en este reto!
summary:
MARS PATHFINDER AI is an interactive scientific expedition planning platform developed by Team GAVILANES for exploring Jezero Crater on Mars.

Our project combines real NASA and United States Geological Survey scientific data with terrain-based route planning to help users design hypothetical astronaut missions. Users can describe their scientific objectives in English or Spanish, select geological samples, configure oxygen, energy, time, and payload constraints, and compare alternative routes calculated using the A* search algorithm.

The platform simulates sample collection, tracks hypothetical resources, and evaluates whether an expedition can return to its base under the selected assumptions. It also provides interactive two-dimensional maps, three-dimensional terrain visualization, experimental augmented reality, and downloadable scientific reports.

By combining authentic Martian terrain, documented Perseverance sampling sites, and transparent simulations, MARS PATHFINDER AI makes planetary exploration more accessible, educational, and interactive while clearly distinguishing scientific measurements from hypothetical human mission parameters.

details:
What We Built

MARS PATHFINDER AI is a bilingual, browser-based scientific expedition planning and simulation platform created by Team GAVILANES for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map.

Our goal is to help users understand the scientific and logistical decisions involved in a hypothetical astronaut expedition on Mars.

Instead of simply displaying a map, the platform allows users to plan a scientific mission, select geological sampling objectives, calculate routes, simulate sample collection, monitor resources, and evaluate whether the astronaut can return to a virtual base.

How It Works

1. Mission Configuration

Users describe their mission in English or Spanish. A local, rule-based language interpreter identifies supported objectives and parameters, including geological material, mission duration, oxygen, energy, reserves, and sample quantities.

The system proposes an editable configuration and requires confirmation before calculating routes. Ambiguous instructions are identified rather than silently interpreted.

2. Scientific Route Planning

The application uses the A* search algorithm to evaluate routes across a numerical digital terrain model of Jezero Crater.

The planner considers terrain elevation, slope limits, available analysis coverage, travel time, hypothetical resource consumption, scientific destinations, and mandatory return to base.

Two strategies are compared: one prioritizes distance, while the other considers an integrated slope penalty. Alternatives are assessed against the mission's configured constraints. The search is bounded and does not claim globally optimal or human-certified routes.

3. Scientific Sample Collection

The platform includes 22 documented historical locations in its source catalog, with 10 classified candidates inside the validated terrain analysis coverage.

Users can plan hypothetical collections of igneous rock, sedimentary rock, and regolith. Historical Perseverance samples remain clearly distinguished from the new samples collected by the simulated astronaut.

4. Mission Simulation

An interactive timeline follows the calculated route, including departure, travel, scientific activities, sample collection, and return.

The system tracks simulated inventory, oxygen, energy, time, and payload capacity. Scientific samples enter the inventory only after the corresponding activity has been completed.

5. Visualization and Reporting

The application includes interactive two-dimensional cartography, three-dimensional terrain derived from numerical elevation data, and experimental WebXR augmented reality on compatible devices.

It also generates downloadable PDF and JSON reports containing mission parameters, route comparisons, scientific objectives, elevation profiles, resource balances, source references, and documented limitations.

Scientific Data

Our platform combines NASA Mars Trek orbital imagery, a United States Geological Survey digital terrain model, NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance sampling records, published geological mapping, and historical atmospheric observations from the Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer.

The original scientific measurements remain separate from hypothetical spacesuit resources, astronaut movement assumptions, simulated sample collection, and virtual base placement.

Technology

The application was developed with React, TypeScript, Vite, OpenLayers, Three.js, React Three Fiber, WebXR, and browser-based PDF generation.

Python-based scientific preprocessing was used to prepare and validate regional terrain and geospatial data. The route planner operates in a Web Worker.

The final application is hosted as a static website on Cloudflare Pages.

Innovation and Impact

Our contribution is the integration of scientific objectives, reproducible terrain-based route planning, interactive expedition simulation, resource evaluation, and multi-dimensional visualization into a single educational platform.

The project is designed to help students and the public explore how geological knowledge, environmental constraints, and mission planning interact during planetary exploration.

Validation and Limitations

The application completed 230 automated tests covering scientific data integrity, route constraints, resource evaluation, sample inventory, language interpretation, visualization controls, and reporting.

The terrain model has a spatial resolution of approximately 20 meters and cannot detect every obstacle relevant to human exploration. Resource consumption and new sample collection are hypothetical. Augmented reality is experimental and requires compatible hardware.

MARS PATHFINDER AI is an educational and exploratory planning system, not a certified astronaut navigation or safety system.

The project was developed with assistance from ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and OpenAI Codex. Scientific data and implementation results were reviewed against documented sources and software tests.
